tries.prompt:
A character model sheet for a narrated animated film, drawn in this art style: our own K1 paper-cut look made minimal, the house look, as the reference image shows it. Every figure and prop is a few flat cut-paper shapes. Every figure and prop has a thick warm dark-brown ink outline and a thin light inner edge just inside it, and is creased once by a single straight diagonal line at the light's angle, its far side a deeper hue of its own colour turned toward violet, never grey and never black. A head is ONE simple shape inside one single thick outline, and the light inner edge runs round that one outline. Garments are flat planes: no pockets, no buttons, no stitching, no seams, no cuffs, no fabric texture. Hands are plain round paper circles at the end of each arm in its sleeve, the sleeve running from the shoulder to the hand: never a hand floating free of the body, never a bare arm, no thumbs, no fingers. Faces are three marks only: two small dark ink oval eyes, short brows and a one-line mouth. One muted hue per piece. The light: a warm, soft key light from the upper left; a soft paper grain on every piece and every plane; a small soft violet contact shadow under each figure, never a darker brown; a muted, warm palette in which only the film's accents are loud. Keep it K1: no white sticker border round the figures, no felt or stitching style, no big glossy eyes, no realistic anatomy. The look is stylised, attractive, expressive and minimal.

Image 1 is the house look: take its paper, its line and its light from it; its hands float free beside the body, which no figure on this sheet does. The person is the apostle Paul as the films draw him: a man of middle age, slight and narrow in build, a little shorter than the other grown men ("his bodily presence is weak", 2 Corinthians 10:10), no halo and no glow. Short dark-brown hair going thin at the crown, with no headcloth; a short dark-brown beard touched with grey, his mouth inside it, parted from the hair by the skin of the cheek; warm tan skin; small dark oval eyes, short dark brows. A plain linen tunic (#d1c6b4) to the ankles with its sleeves to the wrist, and over it a camel travel cloak (#8c7762) about his shoulders, falling to his shins, with no clasp, pattern or trim; brown sandals. Each round hand at the end of its sleeve, no thumbs. His head is one simple shape. What he carries, and only where a pose names it: a reed pen, a sheet or roll of parchment, a small clay oil lamp, a plain staff.

Draw him six times in one row, evenly spaced across the sheet, standing at rest with both arms hanging in their sleeves at the sides, each hand at its sleeve's end, left to right: one, facing the viewer straight on; two, turned three-quarters toward the viewer's left; three, in full profile facing the viewer's left; four, seen from directly behind; five, in full profile facing the viewer's right; six, turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. In profile one eye shows; from behind no face shows, only the back of the hair or headcloth and the garment's back.
